thread:
Maya Singh: heads-up from sync: proposing a "hedge-and-reconcile" pattern to reduce abrupt full rollbacks. flow: local detector -> local gatekeeper -> hedge controller -> router. keep local fast path, global reconciler for escalations.
Arjun Rao: +1. key constraints: keep enforcement idempotent, include decision_id and seq. local can do soft hedges up to 30% by default, anything higher needs global sign-off.
Elena Gomez: add budget tokens per-tenant. hedges consume tokens; if exhausted, escalate. also require at least two orthogonal signals (latency+errors) before escalation.
fallback-bot: notice: staging hedger applied [80->50->20] steps for tenant="delta" region="eu" and logged decision_id=dec-2084-01
Maya Singh: API sketch for RFC: POST /signals (envelope), POST /decisions (gatekeeper->hedger), SSE /decisions/stream. decision event must include: decision_id, tenant, intent(type=params), contributing_signals(list), ttl, issued_by, sequence.
Arjun Rao: tests: simulate observer outage and partial partition. routers must honor TTL and revert when expired. add jitter to ramp to avoid synchronized flips.
Elena Gomez: policy DSL fragment to include: scope(local/global), steps, max_soft_fraction, consecutive_windows, cooldown_secs, required_signals. will draft examples.
Maya Singh: I'll open RFC tomorrow. please add audit metrics: decisions_per_min, avg_signal_to_decision_ms, hedge_success_rate. thanks.
